Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: Biometric data collection includes both fingerprints and iris scans. UNHCR mobile registration teams use biometric iris and fingerprint scanners. The World Bank EAC study notes the card includes a thumbprint image and biographic data. German vendor (MUHLBAUER) supplied the system.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Verified Security Vision wiki entry (documents fingerprint and iris biometric collection under DCRNPI with UNHCR support since 2012) and the World Bank's 2018 EAC mutual-recognition study (thumbprint image plus biographic data on the credential). citizenshiprightsafrica.org could not be refetched (crawl timeout) but its claims are corroborated by the other two sources. A April 2026 Eye Radio report confirms newly deployed mobile registration kits include integrated biometric capture tools, indicating biometric collection continues under the current registration drive. Code 3 rests on documented iris-scan capture (beyond fingerprints only); no source separately confirms a distinct 'facial image' modality, but iris capture is consistent with the higher end of the scale.
revised_comments: South Sudan's Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passport and Immigration (DCRNPI) collects biometric data including fingerprints and iris scans as part of national ID registration, a process supported by UNHCR mobile registration teams since 2012-13. The World Bank's 2018 East African Community study confirms the credential carries a thumbprint image alongside biographic data. Newly deployed mobile registration kits rolled out in 2026 include integrated biometric capture tools, indicating biometric collection remains part of the current registration process. The original system supplier was the German firm Muhlbauer.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: There is a cost to obtain ID credentials. Applicants must pay approximately $20 in fees plus the cost of a blood test and two passport photographs. UNHCR reports this is a barrier for returnees and displaced persons. Revenue collection was previously in cash (now digital via bank in Jan 2026 reform), but costs remain. Birth certificate and witness requirements add further indirect costs.
revision_notes: Confirmed. citizenshiprightsafrica.org could not be refetched (crawl timeout) but the approximate $20 ID fee claim is consistent with wider fee evidence found. Radio Tamazuj (Nov 2024) confirms a nationality card costs SSP 30,000 and passports USD 100-200, and reports MPs rejected a further fee increase. One Citizen Daily (Dec 2024) confirms a revised official fee schedule for civil registry documents effective FY2024/25. Sudans Post (Jan 2026) confirms that as of January 2026 all passport and national ID payments must be made digitally through a bank rather than in cash, but fees are still charged - credentials are not issued free. Code 1 (No) is confirmed on fresher evidence.
revised_comments: Identity credentials in South Sudan are issued for a fee, not free of charge. Applicants pay processing fees for nationality certificates (SSP 30,000 under the 2024/25 fee schedule) and related documents, plus additional costs such as blood tests and passport photographs for national ID applications. Since January 2026, payments for passports and national IDs must be made digitally through a bank-linked system rather than in cash, as part of a Revenue Authority reform intended to reduce informal payments, but the underlying fees remain payable.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Approximately 20% of South Sudan's population (~12 million) have national IDs according to a 2022 official statement. UNHCR estimates ~90% of men, women and children do not possess National ID. The World Bank ID4D dataset (2017) recorded 21% official ID coverage. Low coverage is driven by conflict, displacement, remote populations, and high application costs (~$20 plus blood test and witnesses).
revision_notes: Confirmed, with caveats. The 2022 DCRNPI statement of ~20% coverage remains the most specific figure available; the 2017 World Bank ID4D/EAC study recorded 21%. The World Bank's 2025 Global Findex/ID4D regional brief places South Sudan among seven Sub-Saharan economies with under 60% adult ID ownership but gives no precise updated figure for South Sudan specifically. A January 2026 report (Catholic Radio Network) states the Directorate held 3,080,440 national ID cards 'ready for distribution' under a newly launched ID system requiring adults 18+, which if fully distributed could raise coverage materially; however this describes cards produced/held in stock rather than confirmed issuance to individuals, so it cannot be used to revise the score yet. citizenshiprightsafrica.org could not be refetched (crawl timeout). Code 2 (20-49%) is retained on the best confirmed evidence; the pending mass distribution should be revisited once issuance/uptake data becomes available.
revised_comments: An estimated 20% of South Sudan's population held national identity documents as of 2022, according to the Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passport and Immigration, out of a population of roughly 12 million; this is broadly consistent with the World Bank's 2017 ID4D estimate of 21% ID ownership and with the World Bank's 2025 regional Global Findex brief, which places South Sudan among the Sub-Saharan African countries with under 60% adult ID ownership. Coverage is constrained by conflict, displacement, remote populations and application costs. The government began mass production of new national ID cards in early 2026, with over three million cards reported as printed and awaiting distribution, which may increase coverage once issuance is complete.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: National ID is one of several accepted documents for SIM card registration but not mandatory exclusively. MTN South Sudan accepts: 'Payam Letter, Referendum card, Passport, Driver's license, National ID' for SIM registration. A range of documents are accepted, so the national ID is accepted but not the only option, indicating it is accepted but not mandatory.
revision_notes: Confirmed. MTN South Sudan's SIM registration help page (live) lists the National ID as one of five accepted identification documents (Payam Letter, Referendum card, Passport, Driver's licence, National ID), confirming it is accepted but not the sole/mandatory requirement. A January 2026 Radio Tamazuj report notes DNPI plans a SIM-linked registration system tying foreign residents' permits to mobile numbers, but this concerns non-national residency tracking rather than a change to citizen ID requirements for SIM registration. The LinkedIn source was not refetched as it was not required; MTN's own page is authoritative and sufficient. Code 2 confirmed.
revised_comments: Mobile network operator MTN South Sudan accepts the national ID card as one of several valid identification documents for SIM card registration, alongside a Payam Letter, Referendum card, passport or driver's licence. Because no single document, including the national ID, is mandated exclusively, possession of a national ID is accepted but not required for SIM registration. Separately, authorities have signalled plans for a SIM-linked registration system for foreign residents tying mobile numbers to residency permits.
